vision_report.narrative_description: This chronological botanical audit covers a Mexican Mint seedling in a black pot and a Money Plant cutting in a white cup over a five-day period. In the initial well-lit images (EARLIEST, T-3, T-2), both plants exhibited stable and generally healthy appearances. The Mexican Mint seedling maintained turgid, light green leaves, and the Money Plant cutting displayed a turgid, dark green leaf, though a slight reduction in vibrancy was noted for the Money Plant between EARLIEST and T-3. Soil in the black pot remained moist, and water in the white cup was clear. A critical environmental anomaly, however, occurred between T-2 and T-1, where the overall image lighting drastically diminished and remained extremely low through the CURRENT image. This severe lighting degradation renders precise assessment of plant health, color, and turgidity impossible in the later frames. Despite the poor visibility, no overt signs of collapse or severe deterioration were discernible for either plant. A new, faint reddish object appeared in the upper right of the frame in the CURRENT image, representing an unidentifiable biome anomaly or introduction. The overall health inference is one of stability, but with a medium-low confidence for the latter half of the sequence due to the severe lighting issue.
